summary: The calls support two first-property catalog changes: configure the student application for Homebody Guarantee and enable dynamic pricing for its monthly fee. Most other decisions concern screening rules, claims workflows, coverage, training, and integrations rather than catalog settings. Several implementation details still need confirmation, especially enrollment timing, disclosure text, student-status document collection, charge-code mapping, and lease-addendum setup.

settings.proposed: Configure the online application to ask whether the applicant is a full-time student enrolled in at least nine credit hours and to offer either a traditional guarantor or Homebody Guarantee.
settings.meaning: Eligible students can choose Homebody Guarantee directly within the application instead of supplying a traditional guarantor. Staff can also see the selection in the application record.
settings.assumption: The first property serves student residents and will offer Homebody Guarantee.
reasoning: Leap described application enrollment as a standard Homebody Guarantee workflow.
The full-time-student question controls whether the guarantor-waiver option is shown.
The application must disclose the monthly fee and one-time enrollment fee before the applicant selects the program.

questions.question: Should proof of full-time student status be a required application upload or a required move-in checklist item?
questions.default: Require an application upload on a student-only application; otherwise use an optional upload plus a required move-in checklist item.
questions.why: Leap requires documentary proof for claims, but the Homebody enrollment question only self-certifies student status. A required upload can block nonstudent applicants if the property uses one mixed application.

callsUsed.title: Review Screening Hard code requirements with Leap
callsUsed.brief: Dan, Darren, Austin and Nick from Entrata, along with Yvette from Leap, discussed various underwriting criteria and system functionalities related to rental applications. Key topics included the handling of eviction screenings, the use of Social Security Numbers, the impact of credit scores versus RV index scores, and the implementation of new hard-coded rules for eligibility. The conversation also touched upon potential issues with existing clients using VantageScore and the need for further analysis before implementing broad changes.

callsUsed.title: Yugo Homebody Guaranty Training
callsUsed.brief: Jackie, Joe and Julienne from Entrata, along with KrisAnn, Sarah Simpson, Ginger, Sarah Slife, Makenzi and Yvette, discussed the integration of Homebody Guarantee into Entrata, covering its purpose, application process, and claim filing procedures. Key highlights included the benefits of removing guarantor requirements for renters and providing asset protection for owners, as well as the streamlined claim submission process within Entrata. The teams also addressed coverage limitations, potential future enhancements to the application process, and the need for ongoing training to ensure successful adoption.
customerPeople: Ginger Mathews — Director of Business Systems & Integration

callsUsed.title: Asset HBG Training
callsUsed.brief: Joe Pratt from Entrata, along with Debra from Asset Campus (Sako and Partners), discussed the transition from the LEAP guarantor waiver program to the new Homebody Guarantee integrated within Entrata.
